title: Cross-Platform Tracing and Adaptive Sampler Strategy for Runtime
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood's recommended cross-platform distributed tracing architecture and a standardized adaptive sampling policy for the serving runtime. It describes how to collect correlated traces across user request paths, CPU/GPU kernel executions, and network transfers with bounded overhead, and how to configure adaptive and tail-aware samplers to maximize signal for debugging and regression detection.

Goals:
- Provide a single, operationally simple tracing model that works across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Ensure traces capture: request route, model name and version, batch size, token counts, KV cache hit/miss, kernel ids, GPU kernel durations, and node-level context (NUMA, container id).
- Keep steady-state tracing overhead <= 2% CPU and <= 5ms p50 added latency for typical requests.
- Prioritize collection of rare/high-impact events via tail sampling and adaptive rules.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood serving runtime components: frontend routers, request multiplexer, runtime workers, kernel execution layer, and the Redwood trace agent.
- Includes GPU-level instrumentation (CUPTI/NSYS), kernel telemetry annotations, NIC-level network timing (eBPF), and application-level context propagation (OTel).

Architecture Overview:
- Components:
  - redwood-trace-agent: lightweight sidecar that attaches to each node, collects local spans from the runtime and kernel probes, enriches with node metadata, and forwards to the OTEL collector.
  - otel-collector (shared): receives traces, performs sampling and tail sampling policies, and exports to our trace storage (Jaeger/Tempo + hot index in ClickHouse for fast queries).
  - kernel-probes: modules that emit short GPU/CPU kernel spans with standardized tags (kernel.name, kernel.id, gpu.sm_util_pct, memory_bytes).
  - eBPF collectors: capture NIC transmit/receive microspans and socket-level latencies to correlate network tail effects.

- Trace model conventions (required):
  - root_span: request:<route> with attributes: route, model, model_version, deployment_mode, env, user_token_id (hashed), batch_size, requested_max_tokens, client_latency_ms.
  - child spans: router, multiplexer, kv_cache (hit/miss boolean), kernel:<kernel_name> (with kernel.duration_ms), batching-window, emit-token-loop (per-100-token aggregated span).
  - IDs: span and trace ids must be 128-bit hex. Inject and propagate via W3C Trace-Context headers in HTTP and via metadata across internal gRPC.

Sampling Strategy (high level):
- Default global policy: Probabilistic reservoir sampling at 0.5% for steady-state production traffic. This keeps storage cost bounded while ensuring random coverage.
- Route-priorities: Override probabilistic sampler per-route. Important routes (e.g., admin endpoints, high-RPO customers, new-model routes) should be sampled at higher rates (2–20%).
- Tail-aware sampling: Implement tail-sampler in the OTEL collector that keeps a short window (5m) and promotes traces with high observed latency (> p95), error flags, or kernel anomalies to persisted storage regardless of initial sample decision.
- Adaptive sampler: Dynamically increase sampling for a route when its error rate or tail-latency growth exceeds thresholds. See algorithm below.

Adaptive Sampler Algorithm (pseudocode):
1) For each route R, maintain sliding metrics: rps(R), error_rate(R), tail_latency_p95(R). 5-minute windows.
2) Evaluate every 30s: if error_rate(R) > 0.5% AND rps(R) > 10 => sampler_rate(R) := min(0.2, sampler_rate(R) * 4).
3) If tail_latency_p95(R) increases by >25% vs baseline => sampler_rate(R) := min(0.1, sampler_rate(R) * 2).
4) Decay: every 10 minutes without triggers => sampler_rate(R) := max(default_rate, sampler_rate(R) * 0.7).
5) Ensure a global budget: sum(expected_spans_per_minute) <= configured_limit (configurable per-cluster).

Configuration Reference (OTel collector / redwood-trace-agent):
| key | example | description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| sampling.global_default | 0.005 | global probabilistic default (fraction) |
| sampling.route_overrides | {"/chat/generate":0.02} | per-route overrides as JSON map |
| sampling.tail_window_secs | 300 | window for tail-sampler to keep candidate traces |
| sampling.max_spans_per_min | 50000 | safety budget for a cluster |
| trace_agent.buffer_size_mb | 32 | sidecar memory buffer before backpressure |
| gpu.probe_enabled | true | enable CUPTI/NSYS kernel spans |
| ebpf.nic_capture | drop | capture mode: drop|sample|full (avoid full in prod) |

Operational SLOs and Overhead Targets:
- Trace collection overhead: added p50 latency <= 5ms for normal 16k token requests when sampling <= 1%.
- Collector CPU budget: < 6 vCPU equivalent per 1K qps of traced traffic for full processing.
- Retention tiers: hot traces (30d, high-index) + cold traces (365d, compressed).
- Tail-sampling recall target: capture >= 95% of traces with request latency above configured p99 threshold.

Instrumentation Checklist (developer-facing):
1) Add span entry/exit for each high-level component: request router, multiplexer, model executor, kv-cache check.
2) Annotate spans with these required attributes: model.name, model.version, batch.size, requested_tokens, response_tokens, kv_cache_hit, kernel.id.
3) Emit kernel spans at kernel launch and kernel completion with start_ts and end_ts and resource tags (gpu_index, sm_util).
4) Expose a lightweight debug flag to force-sample traces for a request_id when doing customer debugging.
5) Ensure traces are scrubbed of PII by default; only hashed client ids and truncated prompt previews are allowed.

Rollout Procedure (recommended):
1) Canary: enable redwood-trace-agent on 1% of nodes in a non-prod environment and validate basic end-to-end ingestion.
2) Staged prod rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 1 hour observation windows. Verify overhead metrics after each step.
3) Enable Route overrides incrementally: start with low-risk routes, then business-critical routes.
4) Turn on GPU kernel probes separately: measure overhead with NSYS for 24h before enabling tail-promotion for kernel anomalies.
5) Full tail-sampler enablement only after tail recall verification in a loaded test environment.

Rollback Plan:
- If collector CPU or trace agent memory exceeds thresholds or p50 latency regressions > 10ms observed, roll back to previous sampling global_default and disable GPU/Net probes.
- Use the sidecar healthcheck endpoint (/health/trace-agent) to drain and stop forwarding.

Common troubleshooting patterns and remediation:
- Symptom: Many traces missing kernel spans.
  - Cause: CUPTI permission or probe not loaded on container runtime.
  - Action: Check redwood-trace-agent logs for "gpu-probe: init failed" and ensure container has CAP_SYS_ADMIN or appropriate device access; verify driver/ CUDA version compat.

- Symptom: Sudden spike in trace volume and storage pressure.
  - Cause: misconfigured route override or accidental debug-forced sampling.
  - Action: Temporarily set sampling.global_default to 0.001 and scale down overrides; throttle ingress to collector.

- Symptom: High tail latency captured but not correlated to kernel durations.
  - Cause: Network egress or kv-cache serialization.
  - Action: Enable eBPF NIC microspans for the suspected nodes and re-run tail-sampling for 1 hour.

Diagnostic CLI snippets and examples:
- Force a trace for a single request_id (debug only):
  curl -X POST \
    -H 'X-Redwood-Debug-Force-Trace: request:12345' \
    -d '{"input":"..."}' https://internal-router.local/chat/generate

- Example otel-collector sampling config fragment (YAML):
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        grpc: {}
  processors:
    batch: {}
    tail_sampling:
      policies:
        - name: latency_high
          latency_threshold: 1s
          decision_wait: 30s
  exporters:
    jaeger:
      endpoint: jaeger.internal:14250

- Read GPU kernel spans in ClickHouse (example SQL):
  SELECT trace_id, span_name, kernel_name, span_duration_ms, tags
  FROM traces
  WHERE span_name LIKE 'kernel:%' AND event_ts > now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY
  ORDER BY span_duration_ms DESC
  LIMIT 500;

Appendix A — Minimal agent config example (redwood-trace-agent):
{
  "trace_endpoint": "otel-collector.internal:4317",
  "buffer_mb": 32,
  "sampling": {
    "global_default": 0.005,
    "route_overrides": {"/chat/generate":0.02}
  },
  "gpu_probe": true,
  "ebpf_nic_mode": "sample"
}

Appendix B — Ownership and SLAs:
- Owner: eng-serv-runtime / Observability subteam (primary: Maya Chen).
- SRE oncall: responsible for collector availability and scaling during rollout.
- Expected review cadence: Quarterly review of sampling budgets and route overrides.

Appendix C — Future enhancements (non-blocking):
- Kernel-level histogram sketches exported as metrics to avoid heavy trace storage for frequent short kernels.
- Better correlation between trace spans and token-level cost accounting (token-attribution spans).
- Automatic anomaly detectors that tune sampler rates using Bayesian change point detection.

If you implement or change instrumentation, add an entry to the "profiling-playbook/trace-instrumentation-register" index with components modified, owner, and a short note about expected overhead. For questions, reach out to the Observability channel (#obs-runtime) or directly to the document owner.
